recipes.title: Shakshuka, light
recipes.summary: Eggs poached in a warmly spiced tomato and pepper sauce, loosened with spinach and finished with a little feta.

steps.instruction: Dice the onion and red bell pepper, mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Have the eggs, spinach and feta cheese within reach — once the sauce is ready it moves quickly.

Warm the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and salt and cook, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and translucent and the pepper has lost its raw crunch.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin and smoked paprika. Cook for one minute, until the spices smell toasted — do not let the garlic brown or it will turn bitter.

Tip in the tomatoes, breaking up any large pieces with your spoon. Bring to a gentle simmer and leave uncovered until the sauce thickens enough that a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a brief trail.
Add the spinach a handful at a time, letting each wilt into the sauce before adding the next. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Make four shallow wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover the pan and cook over low heat until the whites are set but the yolks still wobble.
Scatter over the feta cheese and parsley and bring the pan straight to the table.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently under a lid, though the yolks will firm up.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.summary: The classic pan of eggs poached in a rich, smoky tomato and pepper sauce, with feta and bread for mopping.

steps.instruction: Dice the onion and red bell pepper, mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Set the eggs, spinach, feta cheese and white bread nearby.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and salt and cook until the onion is soft and translucent and the pepper is tender.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin and smoked paprika and cook for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, crushing any large pieces. Simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and spoonable rather than watery.
Stir the spinach through in batches until it has wilted completely. Taste and correct the seasoning.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low until the whites are just set.
Finish with the feta cheese and parsley. Serve from the pan with the white bread alongside for scooping up the sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh. The sauce alone keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well — poach fresh eggs into it when you reheat.

recipes.title: Shakshuka, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous skillet of six eggs in a deep spiced tomato sauce, with plenty of feta and enough bread to make a full meal.

steps.instruction: Dice the onion and red bell pepper, mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Have the eggs, spinach, feta cheese and white bread to hand.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, bell pepper and salt until the onion is translucent and the pepper is very tender.
Add the garlic, ground cumin and smoked paprika and stir constantly for a minute until the spices smell toasted.
Pour in the tomatoes and break up any large pieces. Simmer uncovered until thick — a larger pan of sauce takes a little longer to reduce.
Wilt in the spinach a handful at a time, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Make six evenly spaced wells and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Scatter over the feta cheese and parsley and serve from the pan with the white bread.

recipes.storageNotes: Eat fresh. The sauce keeps 3 days without the eggs and reheats well; add fresh eggs at serving time.

recipes.title: Greek yoghurt bowl, light
recipes.summary: Thick Greek yoghurt with berries, a little granola and a drizzle of honey — quick, cold and high in protein.

steps.instruction: Slice the strawberries. Spoon the greek yogurt into a wide bowl and spread it out so every spoonful will pick up some fruit.
Arrange the strawberries and blueberries over the yogurt, scatter over the granola, drizzle with honey and dust with ground cinnamon. Eat straight away while the granola is still crisp.

recipes.storageNotes: Assemble and eat immediately. Fruit and yogurt can sit together in the fridge for a day, but add granola only at the last moment.

recipes.title: Greek yoghurt bowl
recipes.summary: Greek yoghurt topped with strawberries, blueberries, banana, granola, walnuts and honey. Five minutes, no cooking.

steps.instruction: Slice the strawberries and banana and roughly chop the walnuts. Spoon the greek yogurt into a bowl and smooth the surface.

Top with the strawberries, blueberries and banana, then scatter over the granola and walnuts. Drizzle with honey, dust with ground cinnamon and eat immediately for the best contrast of creamy and crunchy.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled just before eating. Prepared fruit keeps a day in the fridge; keep granola and walnuts separate until serving.

recipes.title: Greek yoghurt bowl, hearty
recipes.summary: A big bowl of Greek yoghurt loaded with fruit, granola, walnuts and almond butter — a proper breakfast, not a snack.

steps.instruction: Slice the strawberries and banana and roughly chop the walnuts. Spoon the greek yogurt into a large bowl and spread it wide.
Warm the almond butter briefly if it is stiff, then swirl it through the top of the yogurt in ribbons rather than mixing it in completely.
Arrange the strawberries, blueberries and banana over the top, add the granola and walnuts, drizzle with honey and dust with ground cinnamon. Serve at once.

recipes.storageNotes: Eat immediately for the best texture. Yogurt and cut fruit keep a day; add granola, walnuts and honey only at serving.

recipes.title: Overnight oats, light
recipes.summary: Oats soaked overnight with milk, yoghurt and chia, with plenty of blueberries and just a touch of maple syrup.

steps.instruction: Tip the rolled oats, chia seeds, ground cinnamon and salt into a jar and stir so the chia is evenly spread rather than clumped in one corner.
Add the semi-skimmed milk, greek yogurt and maple syrup. Stir thoroughly, scraping the bottom, until no dry oats remain.
Fold in most of the blueberries, keeping a few back. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least six hours, until the oats are tender and the mixture has thickened.
Stir before eating, loosen with a splash of milk if it has set firmer than you like, and top with the reserved blueberries.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps 2 days covered in the fridge. Stir well and loosen with a little milk before eating. Not suitable for freezing.

recipes.title: Overnight oats
recipes.summary: Creamy blueberry overnight oats with Greek yoghurt, chia and a swirl of almond butter. Made the night before, eaten cold.

steps.instruction: Combine the rolled oats, chia seeds, ground cinnamon and salt in a jar and stir to distribute the seeds evenly.
Pour in the whole milk, greek yogurt and maple syrup and stir until the yogurt is smooth and every oat is wet.
Fold in most of the blueberries, then spoon the almond butter on top and swirl it through lightly rather than mixing it in.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least six hours, until the oats are soft and the chia has thickened everything.
Stir once, top with the remaining blueberries and loosen with a splash of milk if needed.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge, though the texture is best in the first two. Loosen with milk before eating.

recipes.title: Overnight oats, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous jar of overnight oats with extra oats, yoghurt and a proper spoonful of almond butter for a long morning.

steps.instruction: Stir the rolled oats, chia seeds, ground cinnamon and salt together in a large jar so the seeds do not gather in one place.
Add the whole milk, greek yogurt and maple syrup and stir firmly until the yogurt is fully worked in and no dry oats sit at the bottom.
Fold in most of the blueberries, then add the almond butter in small spoonfuls and swirl it through, leaving visible ribbons.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least six hours, until soft and thick.
Stir before serving, loosen with a splash of milk if needed, and finish with the reserved blueberries.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge. Stir well and add milk to loosen. Not suitable for freezing.
